title: Indigenous Kenyan Instrumental Ensembles
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Ensembles need everyone listening. Community examples are for a teacher to confirm.

skills.key_step: The child names kinds of Kenyan ensembles (percussion, string, wind, mixed) and what players do: watch the leader, keep the tempo, balance loudness.

floor.question: Is the litungu string or wind?

steps: Sort the instruments in the group.
Watch the leader and keep together.

board.do: A group has drums, a nyatiti and a horn.

misconceptions.ask: The nyatiti belongs to which kind?
misconceptions.repair: Sort five instruments by how the sound is made.

misconceptions.ask: What should an ensemble player do about loudness?
misconceptions.repair: Play loud together and soft together and compare.

listen_for: Nothing, each plays his own beat
misconceptions.ask: What should players keep together in an ensemble?
misconceptions.repair: Clap in a group, first alone and then together.

misconceptions.ask: How does an ensemble start together?
misconceptions.repair: Start a class clap on a count of four.

checks.question: A group of drums only is which kind of ensemble?
